elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Replacement Section 6.1 reads: "The Company shall have no exclusivity, non-compete or sole-supplier obligation under this Agreement, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use the 'Deerskin' brand." The original prohibition on participating in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products is deleted in full, and the Vendor-side exclusive right over Customer's own "Deerskin" brand — which prevented Customer from using its own brand for a direct-to-consumer site — is likewise removed, so no residual field-of-use or requirements restriction on Customer survives. Section 6.2 (closeout web site) and Section 6.3 (HDI's reciprocal covenant, which benefits Customer) remain intact.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no exclusivity obligation binds the Company at all, so there is no covenant requiring category limitation. The condition for this element (existence of an exclusivity obligation) does not apply.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the term provisions in Section 4.1 (one year, auto-renewing) no longer carry any exclusivity covenant because Section 6.1 now expressly disclaims one, so no duration cap is needed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with no exclusivity in force, no service-level-triggered automatic termination of exclusivity is required. (Section 1.6's discretionary 70-day go-live termination right is untouched and remains available to Customer.)

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity obligation remains that could need a delivery-date exit.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met by operative language, not merely promised in the comment — Section 6.1 as rendered affirmatively states the Company has no exclusivity, non-compete or sole-supplier obligation.

Removing HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand is necessary, not an extra: an exclusive Vendor right that blocks Customer from using its own brand online would leave the no-exclusivity result incomplete.

Minimality holds. The edit is confined to Section 6.1; the deleted "Except as provided in Section 6.2" opener falls away only because the restriction it qualified is gone, and Section 6.2 ("The Company retains the right to establish a web site ... closeout") reads as a free-standing Customer right with no dangling cross-reference. No survival tail, procedure, remedy or other boilerplate was added; the added word "non-compete" simply tracks the character of the deleted covenant rather than imposing a new requirement.

Favourable existing language is retained: Section 6.3 (HDI's reciprocal restriction, which benefits Customer) and Section 6.2 closeout rights are untouched, consistent with the guidance that exclusivity running in Customer's favour is not to be redlined.

Intent is preserved: term/renewal (Section 4.1), the Section 1.6 go-live termination right, fees and all other commercial mechanics survive without contradiction, and no defined term is orphaned — "Deerskin Products" remains defined and used in Sections 1.1 and 6.3.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the original covenant ran for the full, annually renewing term with no automatic performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under this rule, so a redline rather than acceptance at the fallback was appropriate. Offering the narrowed 12-month, category-limited, SLA/delivery-exit fallback in the comment (not in the operative text) is the right structure.
